components.gap: Complete Every Two Elementarily Equivalent Models Have Isomorphic Ultrapowers, 224-233: the exact forward construction and hypotheses are presented in full (Definition 1, Lemmas 1-5, language reduction, bookkeeping function, inductive construction Cases I-VI, parts 1-2 with written proofs; part 3, goodness and the closing remark reported as the source itself leaves them unproved), but Shelah 1971 is not yet complete as a presentation: the content of pp.224-225 outside the theorem statement and notation is not supplied, namely (i) the notation paragraph's assertion that mu is a regular cardinal (p.225), with proof; (ii) Keisler's decomposition of his GCH result into the existence of lambda+-good ultrafilters, lambda+-saturation of ultrapowers by them, and uniqueness of elementarily equivalent saturated models of the same cardinality (p.224, citing Keisler [7],[8], Morley-Vaught [15]); (iii) the alternative approaches of Kochen (ultralimits) and Mansfield (Boolean ultrapowers) (pp.224-225); (iv) the Silver/Rucker consistency result for saturated ultrapowers of countable models and the open question stated on p.225; (v) the stated consequences eliminating GCH from Keisler's characterization of elementary classes and from the Horn-sentence preservation theorem (with Galvin's and Mansfield's earlier eliminations) (p.225). Only the attribution of the Horn converse to Keisler (body line 207-210) and Keisler's GCH version (018 body 138-148) are present.
